messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to perform t-test on two independent samples. We have dataset A: [12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35] (n=10). Dataset B: [14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36] (n=10). We need to compute t-statistic and p-value for alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01. Use two-sided test? Usually t-test. We'll compute mean, variance, pooled variance, t-statistic. Let's compute.

Dataset A: sum = 12+15+18+20+22+25+28+30+32+35 = let's sum: 12+15=27; +18=45; +20=65; +22=87; +25=112; +28=140; +30=170; +32=202; +35=237. So mean_A = 237/10 = 23.7.

Compute sum of squares: we need variance. Compute each deviation squared: (12-23.7)=-11.7 => 136.89; (15-23.7)=-8.7 => 75.69; (18-23.7)=-5.7 => 32.49; (20-23.7)=-3.7 => 13.69; (22-23.7)=-1.7 => 2.89; (25-23.7)=1.3 => 1.69; (28-23.7)=4.3 => 18.49; (30-23.7)=6.3 => 39.69; (32-23.7)=8.3 => 68.89; (35-23.7)=11.3 => 127.69. Sum of squares = let's add: 136.89+75.69=212.58; +32.49=245.07; +13.69=258.76; +2.89=261.65; +1.69=263.34; +18.49=281.83; +39.69=321.52; +68.89=390.41; +127.69=518.10. So variance_A = sumsq/(n-1)=518.10/9=57.5667. Standard deviation_A = sqrt(57.5667)=7.590.

Dataset B: sum = 14+17+19+21+23+26+29+31+33+36 = let's sum: 14+17=31; +19=50; +21=71; +23=94; +26=120; +29=149; +31=180; +33=213; +36=249. Mean_B = 249/10 = 24.9.

Compute deviations: (14-24.9)=-10.9 => 118.81; (17-24.9)=-7.9 => 62.41; (19-24.9)=-5.9 => 34.81; (21-24.9)=-3.9 => 15.21; (23-24.9)=-1.9 => 3.61; (26-24.9)=1.1 => 1.21; (29-24.9)=4.1 => 16.81; (31-24.9)=6.1 => 37.21; (33-24.9)=8.1 => 65.61; (36-24.9)=11.1 => 123.21. Sum squares: 118.81+62.41=181.22; +34.81=216.03; +15.21=231.24; +3.61=234.85; +1.21=236.06; +16.81=252.87; +37.21=290.08; +65.61=355.69; +123.21=478.90. Variance_B = 478.90/9=53.2111. SD_B = sqrt(53.2111)=7.295.

Now compute pooled variance: Sp^2 = ((n1-1)*s1^2 + (n2-1)*s2^2)/(n1+n2-2) = (9*57.5667 + 9*53.2111)/18 = (517. + 478.9)/18? Wait 9*57.5667=518.1003; 9*53.2111=478.8999. Sum=996.9999. Divide by 18 = 55.4444. So Sp = sqrt(55.4444)=7.44.

Standard error of difference: SE = Sp * sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2) = 7.44 * sqrt(0.1 + 0.1) = 7.44 * sqrt(0.2) = 7.44 * 0.4472136 = 3.327.

t-statistic = (mean_A - mean_B)/SE = (23.7 - 24.9)/3.327 = (-1.2)/3.327 = -0.3608. Absolute t = 0.3608.

Degrees of freedom = n1+n2-2 = 18.

Now we need p-value for two-sided test. For t=0.3608, df=18. The p-value is 2*(1 - CDF_t(|t|)). We can approximate using t distribution. For small t, p-value ~ 0.72? Let's approximate: t=0.36, df=18. The t critical values: t0.05 two-sided df=18: about 2.101. t0.01 two-sided df=18: about 2.878. Our t is far less than both, so p-value > 0.05. Let's compute approximate p-value: Using t distribution table: For df=18, t=0.36, the one-sided p-value maybe around 0.36? Actually t=0.36 is very small, so p-value close to 0.72? Let's approximate using normal: For large df, t approximates normal. For t=0.36, normal two-sided p-value = 2*(1 - Phi(0.36)) = 2*(1 - 0.6406) = 2*0.3594 = 0.7188. So p ~ 0.72. So not significant at 0.05 or 0.01.

Thus results: t = -0.361, df=18, p ≈ 0.72. So fail to reject null at both alpha levels.
